benmore api --help prints local help and exits 0; flag-like app arguments are usage errors (2).
A positional `.` resolves through the current workspace's .benmore/app marker. Outside a pulled workspace, pass the deployed app name explicitly.
benmore open [app] uses the authenticated app list and chooses a provisioned dev URL when no environment is pinned; explicit --env dev|prod wins.

benmore sync-status intentionally keeps its separate 0 clean / 1 drift / 2 conflict / 3 setup contract; do not feed those statuses through the generic mapping. `benmore deploy` and `benmore delete-file` share two of those codes for their manifest guard: 2 when the deployed source conflicts with the local base (also their usage code), 3 when the manifest check could not run.

Every hosted command checks its flags before it signs in or sends anything. A flag the command does not take is refused with exit 2 (sync-status: 3), a did-you-mean hint and the flags it accepts (`benmore probe app POST /x --data '{}'` -> unknown flag --data (did you mean --body?)); a value flag without a value and `--bool=value` are refused the same way. `--flag=value` works wherever `--flag value` does. `benmore probe` also refuses a fourth positional argument.
`--help` or `-h` anywhere before `--` prints the command's usage and exits 0 without running it (`benmore create-app myapp --help`, `benmore disable myapp -h`). `benmore help <command>` is the same.

A platform 4xx or 503 answer prints the platform's own message after the status, so a stopped app reads `error: Error 503: The app is not running, so its data can't be shown. Start or restart it ...` (fix: `benmore restart <app>`) and a refusal reads `error: Error 403: access denied ...`. That message is the `error`, `message` and `hint` strings of a JSON error body, joined on one line, control and bidi characters removed and cut at 500 characters; a body over 64 KiB is not read as a message. 4xx and 503 messages are written for the caller (what was refused and what to do) and are the same text the MCP tools return. Every other 5xx, and any body that is not a JSON object (a proxy's HTML page, plain text), prints only `Error <status>`, because a 500 body can carry internal error text. Every hosted command prints it the same way, including those that look up the app list, the source manifest, `benmore pull`, `benmore logs`, `benmore env` and the MCP-backed commands. A 401 prints the sign-in text and an ambiguous app name its own text; exit codes follow the mapping above (2/4/5/1).

`benmore` and `benmore help` print the common workflows (start, existing app, change and check, release) with each command labelled inspect, local, change or promote; `benmore help all` prints every command grouped by effect, and `benmore help <command>` one command.

push, deploy, delete-file, `sql --write` and promote print `target: <command> → app <app>, environment <env> (<source>)` on stderr before sending anything; the source is --env, the `benmore use` pin, or the app's default (dev when it has one, else prod, read from your app list), so an unpinned push to an app with no dev instance says that it lands in production. The line never goes to stdout. The save hook (`push --from-claude-hook`) prints it only when its push lands in prod; a trailing `-dev` on the app is dropped and an `--env` other than dev or prod exits 2 before sending; a first deploy prints the line before it creates the app.
A selector flag (--app, --app-dir, --env, --dir) given twice with different values is refused with exit 2 (sync-status: 3) before anything runs.

`benmore deploy` writes its progress lines (creating, deploying, the iterate hint) to stderr; stdout keeps only the result line with the URL. `benmore apps` reports a network failure and `not logged in` on stderr.
